title: OFFDAY · sparkling tea

sources.title: Pentagram — EBBS
sources.role: Observed large type, restrained color and a consistent identity across cylindrical packaging. Our OFFDAY concept uses different names, colors and artwork.

review: Two coordinated cans have distinct coral and powder-blue flavor labels. Wordmarks, flavor names and 355 ml marks are readable. Aluminum rims, paper labels and shadows have distinct material behavior.
limitations: A visual packaging concept. It does not include a dieline, ingredient panel or a print-ready label file.
technique: Define the shared identity once, then specify exactly what changes between product variants.

title: OFFDAY · good tea, zero plans

sources.title: Pentagram — EBBS
sources.role: Observed large type, restrained color and a consistent identity across cylindrical packaging. Our OFFDAY concept uses different names, colors and artwork.

review: The coral can retains its wordmark, emblem, flavor and volume. The large two-line headline is exact and does not overlap the product. Blue, white and coral create a coherent campaign image.
limitations: The can was redrawn from the reference rather than composited pixel for pixel. Tiny label geometry and finish can change. No advertising performance was tested.
technique: Attach the product reference, reserve a separate copy zone and list the label details to preserve.

title: OFFDAY · wear the identity

sources.title: Pentagram — EBBS
sources.role: Observed large type, restrained color and a consistent identity across cylindrical packaging. Our OFFDAY concept uses different names, colors and artwork.

review: The white tee, blue tote and coral tag form one clear flat lay. The wordmark and eye-shaped emblem carry across with appropriate black or white ink. Knit, canvas, seams and print have convincing texture.
limitations: The logo proportions are approximate across curved and folded material. These are mockups; no garment pattern or production artwork is included.
technique: Transfer the identity while specifying the physical surfaces, ink colors and exact item count.

title: OFFDAY · the core mark

sources.title: Pentagram — EBBS
sources.role: Observed large type, restrained color and a consistent identity across cylindrical packaging. Our OFFDAY concept uses different names, colors and artwork.

review: The mark is isolated into a clear vertical lockup: one black almond shape with a circular negative-space opening above the condensed wordmark. The composition is legible without supporting imagery.
limitations: A raster identity concept, not a vector master or a trademark-clearance result. Fine contours, kerning and the background retain small raster variations.
technique: Ask to extract the identity from the reference and remove the product context.

title: Listening room · six pictograms

sources.title: IBM Design Language — pictogram design
sources.role: Reference for consistent geometry, stroke logic and a readable pictogram family; no source pictograms attached.

review: All six requested symbols are recognizable in a three-by-two arrangement: headphones, turntable, mixer, reel deck, metronome and speaker. The targeted cleanup reduced surface noise while retaining the composition and red accents.
limitations: Cleanup was only partial: faint mottling remains in the navy and red. Stroke weight and optical size are not perfectly uniform. Treat this as a family direction; rebuild approved symbols as vectors for a production icon library.
technique: Name every symbol, set a shared geometric language and inspect the whole family rather than one icon alone.

title: The afternoon rehearsal

sources.title: Malika Favre — The Travel Editions
sources.role: Observed limited palettes, negative space and clear silhouettes. The pianist composition is an original brief; no source artwork attached.

review: A single pianist, large piano silhouette and diagonal window light create a strong editorial composition. The restrained ivory, navy, black and red palette gives the scene a coherent mood.
limitations: The output adds subtle shading and detailed piano strings beyond the requested flat shapes. Piano geometry and mechanics are stylized, not technically verified.
technique: Describe the silhouette, viewpoint and negative space first; use a limited palette to organize the scene.
